questions.question: A body travels 10 m east and then 6 m west. The distance and displacement are respectively
questions.explanation: Distance = total path length = 10 + 6 = 16 m. Displacement = net change in position = 10 − 6 = 4 m east.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is always TRUE?
questions.explanation: Distance (a path length) is at least as large as the magnitude of the displacement (the shortest straight-line). Equality holds only when motion is in one direction without retracing.

questions.question: The slope of the position-time (x-t) graph gives
questions.explanation: Velocity is dx/dt — the slope of the x-t graph at any point is the instantaneous velocity.

questions.question: A body moves with uniform velocity. Its acceleration is
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity means velocity is unchanging, so the rate of change of velocity (acceleration) is zero.

questions.question: A body has positive velocity and negative acceleration. Which is true?
questions.explanation: Velocity and acceleration of opposite sign means the body is decelerating — its speed decreases until it eventually reverses direction.

questions.question: The SI unit of acceleration is
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity / time = (m/s) / s = m/s².

questions.question: A body starts from rest with uniform acceleration 4 m/s². Its velocity after 5 s is
A body starts from rest with uniform acceleration 2 m/s². The distance covered in 5 s is
A car decelerates uniformly from 30 m/s to rest over a distance of 90 m. Its deceleration is
questions.explanation: Use v² = u² − 2as: 0 = 900 − 2a(90) ⇒ a = 5 m/s².

questions.question: A body moves with velocity v(t) = 3t² m/s. Its acceleration at t = 2 s is
questions.explanation: a = dv/dt = 6t. At t = 2, a = 12 m/s².

questions.question: The kinematic equation v² = u² + 2as is valid
options: only when acceleration is constant in magnitude and direction
only when initial velocity is zero
questions.answer: only when acceleration is constant in magnitude and direction
questions.explanation: All three kinematic equations are derived under the assumption of constant acceleration. They fail for variable acceleration.

questions.question: A stone is dropped from rest from a 20-m high tower. The time it takes to reach the ground is (g = 10 m/s²)
A stone is dropped from rest from a 45-m high tower. Its velocity just before hitting the ground is (g = 10 m/s²)
A ball is thrown vertically upward with 20 m/s. Maximum height reached is (g = 10 m/s²)
A ball is thrown vertically upward with 20 m/s. Total time of flight (up and back to launch height) is (g = 10 m/s²)
The area under a v-t graph between two times represents
questions.explanation: The area under a velocity-time graph between t₁ and t₂ equals the displacement during that interval.

questions.question: The slope of a velocity-time graph gives
questions.explanation: Acceleration is dv/dt — the slope of the v-t graph.

questions.question: On a v-t graph for uniformly accelerated motion starting from rest, the curve is
options: a straight line through origin with positive slope
questions.answer: a straight line through origin with positive slope
questions.explanation: v = at: linear in t, slope a, passes through origin. The position curve x = (1/2)at² is the parabola.

questions.question: On an x-t graph for uniformly accelerated motion starting from rest, the curve is
questions.explanation: x = (1/2)at² — quadratic in t, so it's an upward-opening parabola from origin.

questions.question: For a body moving with uniform velocity, the position-time graph is
options: a straight line with non-zero slope
questions.answer: a straight line with non-zero slope
questions.explanation: Uniform velocity ⇒ x = vt + x₀, linear in t with slope v.

questions.question: For a body at rest, the position-time graph is
questions.explanation: x is constant, so the graph is a horizontal line at that x value.

questions.question: An object covers 20 m in the 3rd second and 30 m in the 5th second. The uniform acceleration is
questions.explanation: S_n = u + a(n − 1/2). S_3 = u + 2.5a = 20 and S_5 = u + 4.5a = 30. Subtracting: 2a = 10 ⇒ a = 5 m/s².

questions.question: If displacement is zero, distance is also zero.
questions.explanation: Zero displacement can occur even with non-zero distance — e.g. one lap around a track returns you to the starting point. Distance = 400 m, displacement = 0.

questions.question: Speed can be negative.
questions.explanation: Speed is the magnitude of velocity — always non-negative. Velocity can be negative (indicates direction in 1D).

questions.question: If the velocity of a body is zero at some instant, its acceleration must also be zero at that instant.
questions.explanation: Velocity zero does NOT imply acceleration zero. Example: a stone at the apex of a vertical throw has v = 0 but acceleration g downward.

questions.question: In free fall, two bodies of different mass dropped from the same height reach the ground at the same time (air resistance neglected).
questions.explanation: All freely falling bodies have the same acceleration g, independent of mass. Time to fall depends only on the height.

questions.question: The area under an acceleration-time (a-t) graph gives the change in velocity.
questions.explanation: Δv = ∫a dt, which is the area under the a-t curve.

questions.question: The vector quantity that represents the change in position of a body is called its ____.
questions.explanation: Displacement is the vector from initial to final position; distance is the scalar path length.

questions.question: For uniformly accelerated motion, v = u + ____.
questions.explanation: First kinematic equation: final velocity = initial velocity + acceleration × time.

questions.question: For uniformly accelerated motion, s = ut + ____.
questions.explanation: Second kinematic equation: displacement = ut + (1/2) a t².

questions.question: For uniformly accelerated motion, v² = u² + ____.
questions.explanation: Third kinematic equation: v² − u² = 2as.

questions.question: Near Earth's surface, the acceleration due to gravity is approximately ____ m/s² (downward).
questions.explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (often rounded to 10 m/s² for estimates).

questions.question: The area under a velocity-time graph between t₁ and t₂ represents the ____.
questions.explanation: ∫v dt over [t₁, t₂] = displacement.

questions.question: Define distance and displacement with one example showing they can differ.
questions.answer: Distance is the total path length covered by a body (scalar, ≥ 0). Displacement is the change in position (vector, magnitude = straight-line distance from start to end). Example: a runner runs 200 m east and then 50 m west — distance = 250 m, displacement = 150 m east.

questions.question: Distinguish average speed from average velocity.
questions.answer: Average speed = total distance / total time (scalar, ≥ 0). Average velocity = total displacement / total time (vector). For motion along a straight line in one direction they have equal magnitudes; for round-trip motion the average speed is non-zero while the average velocity can be zero.

questions.question: Can a body have positive velocity and negative acceleration at the same instant? Give an example.
questions.answer: Yes. Velocity and acceleration can have opposite signs — this means the body is decelerating. Example: a car moving forward (+v) while applying the brakes (−a) is slowing down; eventually it stops, and if a continues it would reverse the motion.

questions.question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 10 seconds. Find (i) its final velocity, (ii) the distance covered, (iii) its average velocity during this period.
questions.answer: (i) v = u + at = 0 + 2 × 10 = 20 m/s. (ii) s = ut + (1/2) a t² = 0 + (1/2) × 2 × 100 = 100 m. (iii) Average velocity = total displacement / total time = 100 / 10 = 10 m/s (which equals (u + v)/2 since acceleration is constant).

questions.question: A train moving at 20 m/s comes to rest in 10 s on applying the brakes. Find (i) the deceleration, (ii) the distance covered before coming to rest.
questions.answer: (i) v = u + at ⇒ 0 = 20 + a × 10 ⇒ a = −2 m/s². Deceleration = 2 m/s². (ii) v² = u² + 2as ⇒ 0 = 400 − 4s ⇒ s = 100 m.

questions.question: A body covers 40 m in the 4th second and 60 m in the 6th second of its motion under uniform acceleration. Find the initial velocity and the acceleration.
questions.answer: Using S_n = u + a(n − 1/2): S_4 = u + 3.5a = 40; S_6 = u + 5.5a = 60. Subtracting: 2a = 20 ⇒ a = 10 m/s². Then u = 40 − 3.5 × 10 = 5 m/s.

questions.question: State the conditions under which the three kinematic equations v = u + at, s = ut + (1/2)at², v² = u² + 2as can be applied.
questions.answer: The three equations are valid ONLY if (i) the acceleration is constant in magnitude AND direction throughout the interval of interest, (ii) motion is along a straight line. If a varies with time or the body changes direction, these equations fail and a more general (often integral) approach is needed.

questions.question: A stone is thrown vertically upward with initial velocity 30 m/s. Find (i) maximum height reached, (ii) time to reach maximum height, (iii) total time of flight (back to launch height). (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: (i) h_max = u² / (2g) = 900 / 20 = 45 m. (ii) Time to apex: t_up = u/g = 30/10 = 3 s. (iii) Total time of flight: T = 2u/g = 60/10 = 6 s.

questions.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 80 m. Take g = 10 m/s². Find (i) the time to reach the ground, (ii) the velocity just before hitting the ground.
questions.answer: (i) h = (1/2) g t² ⇒ 80 = 5 t² ⇒ t = 4 s. (ii) v = g t = 10 × 4 = 40 m/s downward (or use v² = 2gh = 1600 ⇒ v = 40 m/s).

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward from the top of a 25-m tall building with initial speed 20 m/s. Find the total time taken to reach the ground at the foot of the building. (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.answer: Take up as positive, building top as origin. Displacement of the ground = −25 m. Use s = ut − (1/2) g t² ⇒ −25 = 20 t − 5 t² ⇒ 5 t² − 20 t − 25 = 0 ⇒ t² − 4 t − 5 = 0 ⇒ (t − 5)(t + 1) = 0. So t = 5 s (positive root).

questions.question: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent? What about the slope?
questions.answer: Area under a v-t curve = displacement during that interval (with sign — positive areas above the t-axis, negative below). Slope of a v-t curve at any instant = acceleration at that instant.

questions.question: Sketch (in words) the position-time graph for (i) a body at rest, (ii) a body moving with uniform velocity, (iii) a body moving with uniform acceleration from rest.
questions.answer:
(i) A body at rest: horizontal line — x stays constant.
(ii) Uniform velocity: straight line with constant positive (or negative) slope, passing through (0, x₀).
(iii) Uniform acceleration from rest: an upward-opening parabola starting at the origin (x = (1/2) a t²); slope increases linearly with time.

questions.question: Two cars start from the same point. Car A moves with uniform velocity 10 m/s. Car B starts from rest with acceleration 2 m/s². Describe (in words) the shape of each car's x-t graph and whether they ever meet again.
questions.answer: Car A: straight line through origin with slope 10. Car B: upward parabola through origin (x = t²). Initially A is ahead (linear grows faster than t² near t=0), but B catches up — set 10 t = t² ⇒ t = 10 s. They meet at t = 10 s, x = 100 m. Beyond that point, B (the parabola) outruns A (the straight line).

questions.question: Derive the three kinematic equations of motion (v = u + at, s = ut + (1/2)at², v² = u² + 2as) for a body moving with uniform acceleration along a straight line.
questions.answer:
Let initial velocity = u, constant acceleration = a, final velocity after time t = v, displacement during this time = s.

(1) Definition of acceleration: a = (v − u)/t ⇒ v = u + at. (First equation.)

(2) Average velocity for uniform acceleration: v̄ = (u + v)/2. Displacement: s = v̄ × t = (u + v) t / 2. Substitute v = u + at: s = (u + u + at) t / 2 = ut + (1/2) a t². (Second equation.)

(3) From (1): t = (v − u)/a. Substitute into (2): s = (u + v)(v − u) / (2a) = (v² − u²) / (2a). Rearranging: v² = u² + 2 a s. (Third equation.)

All three are valid only when a is constant in magnitude and direction throughout the interval.

questions.question: A ball is thrown vertically upward with an initial velocity of 25 m/s from the top of a 30-m tall building. Take g = 10 m/s². Find (a) the maximum height the ball reaches above the ground, (b) the velocity of the ball when it returns to the level of the rooftop, (c) the total time of flight before it strikes the ground.
questions.answer:
Take up as positive; let the rooftop be the origin. Ground is at y = −30.

(a) Maximum height above rooftop: H = u²/(2g) = 625/20 = 31.25 m. Above ground = 31.25 + 30 = 61.25 m.

(b) At rooftop again, the ball's velocity has the same magnitude but opposite direction: 25 m/s downward. (By energy conservation or by applying v² = u² − 2g·0 = u².)

(c) Total time to reach ground: −30 = 25 t − 5 t² ⇒ 5 t² − 25 t − 30 = 0 ⇒ t² − 5 t − 6 = 0 ⇒ (t − 6)(t + 1) = 0 ⇒ t = 6 s.

questions.question: Using a velocity-time graph, derive the equation s = ut + (1/2)at² for uniformly accelerated motion.
questions.answer:
Plot v on the vertical axis vs t on the horizontal. For uniform acceleration, the v-t graph is a straight line from (0, u) to (t, v) where v = u + at.

The displacement s is the area under this line between t = 0 and t = t. This area is a trapezium with parallel sides u and v and width t:

s = (1/2) × (u + v) × t = (1/2) (u + (u + at)) t = (1/2) (2u + at) t = ut + (1/2) a t².

Alternatively split the area into a rectangle (height u, width t, area = ut) and a triangle (base t, height at, area = (1/2) × t × at = (1/2) at²). Summing gives the same result.

questions.question: A particle moves along a straight line. Its position-time graph shows three phases: (i) 0 to 5 s, uniform velocity of +10 m/s; (ii) 5 to 10 s, uniform acceleration of −2 m/s²; (iii) 10 to 20 s, uniform velocity. Find the particle's velocity in phase (iii) and the total displacement over 20 s.
questions.answer:
Phase (i): velocity = +10 m/s for 5 s. Displacement = 10 × 5 = 50 m.

Phase (ii): u = 10, a = −2, t = 5. Final velocity v = 10 + (−2)(5) = 0 m/s. Displacement during this phase = ut + (1/2) a t² = 50 + (1/2)(−2)(25) = 50 − 25 = 25 m.

Phase (iii): velocity is constant at 0 m/s (the value at the end of phase ii). Displacement = 0 × 10 = 0 m.

Total displacement = 50 + 25 + 0 = 75 m. Velocity in phase (iii) = 0 m/s.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A car travelling at 20 m/s applies its brakes uniformly and comes to rest in 4 s.

(i) Find the deceleration of the car.
(ii) Find the distance covered while braking.
(iii) If the same braking is applied at 40 m/s, how long would the car take to stop?
(iv) How does the stopping distance change between (ii) and (iii)?
questions.answer:
(i) v = u + at ⇒ 0 = 20 + a × 4 ⇒ a = −5 m/s². Deceleration = 5 m/s².
(ii) s = (u + v) t / 2 = 20 × 4 / 2 = 40 m. (Or v² = u² + 2as ⇒ s = 40 m.)
(iii) v = u + at ⇒ 0 = 40 − 5 t ⇒ t = 8 s.
(iv) s = u² / (2|a|) = 1600 / 10 = 160 m — four times the stopping distance at half the speed. (Stopping distance ∝ u²: doubling speed quadruples the distance.)

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A stone is dropped from a 125-m cliff. At the same instant, another stone is thrown vertically downward from the same point with initial velocity 5 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s².

(i) Find the time the dropped stone takes to reach the ground.
(ii) Find the time the thrown stone takes to reach the ground.
(iii) What is the difference in their arrival times?
(iv) What is the velocity of each stone just before impact?
questions.answer:
(i) Dropped stone: 125 = (1/2)(10) t² ⇒ t² = 25 ⇒ t = 5 s.
(ii) Thrown stone: 125 = 5t + 5t² ⇒ t² + t − 25 = 0 ⇒ t = (−1 + √101)/2 ≈ (−1 + 10.05)/2 ≈ 4.52 s.
(iii) Δt ≈ 5 − 4.52 ≈ 0.48 s. The thrown stone reaches the ground about half a second earlier.
(iv) Dropped: v = √(2 g h) = √2500 = 50 m/s. Thrown: v² = 5² + 2 × 10 × 125 = 25 + 2500 = 2525 ⇒ v ≈ 50.25 m/s. Both very close — the head start matters more for time than for impact speed.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A ball is thrown vertically upward from the ground with initial velocity 40 m/s. Take g = 10 m/s².

(i) Find the maximum height reached.
(ii) Find the time to reach maximum height.
(iii) Find the velocity at half the maximum height (on the way UP).
(iv) Find the time at which the ball is at a height of 60 m (give both answers — on the way up and on the way down).

Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A scooter accelerates uniformly from rest at 1.5 m/s² for 20 seconds, then moves at constant velocity for the next 30 seconds.

(i) Find the velocity at the end of the accelerating phase.
(ii) Find the distance covered during the accelerating phase.
(iii) Find the distance covered during the constant-velocity phase.
(iv) Find the total distance and the average speed over the 50-second motion.

Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A particle's velocity-time graph is described as follows: v = 0 at t = 0; v increases linearly to 10 m/s at t = 5 s; v stays at 10 m/s from t = 5 to t = 15 s; v decreases linearly to 0 at t = 20 s.

(i) Find the acceleration during 0 to 5 s.
(ii) Find the acceleration during 5 to 15 s.
(iii) Find the acceleration during 15 to 20 s.
(iv) Find the total displacement during 0 to 20 s.
questions.answer:
(i) a = Δv/Δt = (10 − 0)/(5 − 0) = 2 m/s².
(ii) a = 0 (velocity constant).
(iii) a = (0 − 10)/(20 − 15) = −2 m/s² (deceleration).
(iv) Total displacement = total area under v-t graph. Three pieces: triangle from 0 to 5 (area = (1/2)(5)(10) = 25 m), rectangle from 5 to 15 (area = 10 × 10 = 100 m), triangle from 15 to 20 (area = (1/2)(5)(10) = 25 m). Total = 25 + 100 + 25 = 150 m.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Three cars start moving from the same point at the same time along a straight road. Car A moves with constant velocity 15 m/s; Car B starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s²; Car C moves with constant velocity 10 m/s.

(i) Describe the shape of each car's position-time graph.
(ii) After how many seconds does Car B overtake Car A?
(iii) At what time and position does Car B overtake Car C?
(iv) Which car is the fastest at t = 5 s?
questions.answer:
(i) A: straight line through origin, slope 15. B: parabola through origin, x = t². C: straight line through origin, slope 10.
(ii) B overtakes A when t² = 15t ⇒ t = 15 s (and x = 225 m).
(iii) B overtakes C when t² = 10t ⇒ t = 10 s, x = 100 m.
(iv) Velocities at t = 5 s: A = 15 m/s, B = 2 × 5 = 10 m/s, C = 10 m/s. Car A is fastest.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A hot-air balloon is rising vertically at a constant speed of 5 m/s. When the balloon is at a height of 40 m above the ground, a small object is released from the basket. Take g = 10 m/s², up as positive.

(i) What is the initial velocity of the object the moment it is released?
(ii) What is the maximum height the object reaches above the ground?
(iii) How long does the object take to reach the ground after being released?
(iv) What is the velocity of the object just before it hits the ground?
questions.answer:
(i) The object inherits the balloon's velocity at release: +5 m/s (upward).
(ii) From release height 40 m, the object continues upward by u²/(2g) = 25/20 = 1.25 m. Max height = 40 + 1.25 = 41.25 m.
(iii) Equation from release point: −40 = 5 t − 5 t² ⇒ 5 t² − 5 t − 40 = 0 ⇒ t² − t − 8 = 0 ⇒ t = (1 + √33)/2 ≈ (1 + 5.745)/2 ≈ 3.37 s.
(iv) v = u − g t = 5 − 10 × 3.37 ≈ −28.7 m/s. So the object hits the ground at ~28.7 m/s downward.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A particle moves along the x-axis with x(t) = 5t³ − 30t² + 60 t. Position is in metres, time in seconds.

(i) Find the velocity as a function of time.
(ii) Find the acceleration as a function of time.
(iii) At what time is the velocity zero?
(iv) At that instant, is the particle accelerating or decelerating?
questions.answer:
(i) v(t) = dx/dt = 15 t² − 60 t + 60 m/s.
(ii) a(t) = dv/dt = 30 t − 60 m/s².
(iii) v = 0 ⇒ 15 t² − 60 t + 60 = 0 ⇒ t² − 4 t + 4 = 0 ⇒ (t − 2)² = 0 ⇒ t = 2 s.
(iv) At t = 2 s, a = 30 × 2 − 60 = 0 m/s². So the particle has zero velocity AND zero acceleration at that instant. It is momentarily neither accelerating nor decelerating — this is an inflection-style point of the motion.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

A train is moving with a uniform velocity of 72 km/h. It applies its brakes and comes to rest in a distance of 200 m.

(i) Convert 72 km/h to m/s.
(ii) Find the uniform deceleration of the train.
(iii) Find the time the train takes to come to rest.
(iv) Find the distance covered in the first half of the braking time.
questions.answer:
(i) 72 km/h = 72 × 1000 / 3600 = 20 m/s.
(ii) v² = u² + 2as ⇒ 0 = 400 + 2a × 200 ⇒ a = −1 m/s². Deceleration = 1 m/s².
(iii) v = u + at ⇒ 0 = 20 − t ⇒ t = 20 s.
(iv) First half = 10 s. s = ut + (1/2) a t² = 20 × 10 − (1/2) × 1 × 100 = 200 − 50 = 150 m. (So 150 m of the 200 m is covered in the first half of the time — most of the distance is covered while the train is still going fast.)
